title: ÆTHER: Monsoon Duel v2 (the rain and the blades play the music)
maker: ElevenLabs Music API on the owner's paid plan

positive_global_styles: a cinematic martial-arts duel score in pouring monsoon rain, built from the scene's own sounds, composed like a senior blockbuster film composer, not a DJ mix
D minor, Carnatic raga feel with gamakam slides, about 132 BPM
the rain is an instrument: raindrops falling on a Kerala bell-metal vessel and on a steel sword blade ring as tuned bell notes that play the melody
the swords play the hook: every blade clash is a tuned, ringing metallic note of the 5-note signature riff
a limping, circling 7-beat Kerala rhythm counted 3+2+2 on chenda and edakka, pitched-down mridangam as deep sub hits
a Kerala kombu war horn cries out like a battle call
balanced fusion: real chenda, edakka, veena, strings and low brass share the spotlight equally with fresh electronics (gritty synth lead, glitch-chopped veena, deep melodic sub bass)
clean, tonal, wide, punchy cinematic mix with big transients

positive_local_styles: the very first sound: a Kerala kombu horn cries out and bends upward over one deep thunder boom

then only two sounds: raindrops on a bell-metal vessel ring tuned notes that play a rising 3-note call (root, minor third, fifth, the last note held and bent up), and a sword blade rings the same notes, over a soft low drone
an edakka talking drum bends its pitch and sings the 5-note signature riff, the tuned raindrops answer it
the limping 7-beat rhythm (3+2+2) starts softly on chenda rim taps like circling footsteps, then a glitch-chopped veena joins, then a deep melodic sub bass enters at the end
one reversed veena swell into a massive blade clash hit, then the full duel groove in 7 lands: thunderous chenda, tuned sword clashes ringing the riff, low brass, racing string counter-melody
a call-and-response duel: the chenda plays a phrase, a gritty synth lead answers it, faster and faster
surprise: the whole band and the rain stop dead
in slow motion, single heavy raindrops fall one by one, each drop rings one note of the signature riff on bell metal, over a held low hum
a thunder crack and the whole band slams back in up a whole step, the rhythm switches from the limping 7 to a straight, driving double-time 4
wordless warrior chants shout the signature riff, brass and tuned sword clashes play it with them
an interlude showpiece over the held groove: the edakka and a violin trade the riff with Carnatic gamakam slides, faster and faster, chenda rolls building underneath
one final massive unison hit with a thunder crack and a deep sub drop, then silence
only the rain returns, and the sword blade rings the rising 3-note call one last time, slower, the last note held and bent up

brief.notes: Jithesh 29 Oct 16:35 on v1: 'Nothing unique in it' (it was a generic epic chenda + brass + choir cue). v2 builds the track from the scene's own sounds, like Red Line did with the car: (1) rain drops on a Kerala bell-metal uruli and a ringing sword blade are TUNED and play the melody; (2) every blade clash is a note of the hook (the swords play the riff); (3) a Kerala kombu war-horn cry is the attention grab; (4) the duel groove is a limping 7-beat Kerala rhythm (3+2+2) that switches to a straight driving 4 at the storm break; (5) surprise: time stops and single slow-motion raindrops ring the hook one note at a time. Mr. Raga rules kept: 1-2 sound mystery open, layer-by-layer build, about half real instruments and half fresh electronics, a hook at every 8-12 s change, one reversed-veena swell, Hopeverse motif at start and end, composed transitions.

story: Two Kalari warriors face each other in monsoon rain. Time stops between drops, then the storm breaks.
human_work: to be added by the owner: melody, take choice, edits, mix
